circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, designed by Hermann Tilke and located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, spans 5. 281 kilometers and has been the traditional season finale for Formula One since 2009. The track represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, serves as a street course encircling Albert Park Lake and hosts the annual Australian Grand Prix along with various supporting racing series. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, meeting the highest safety and facility standards for international motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods in its history. Originally operating as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, the track underwent modifications and rebranding as the A1-Ring before resuming Grand Prix racing from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest F1 track globally. After hosting the 2016 European Grand Prix as its inaugural Formula One event, the venue shifted to become the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Bahrain International Circuit, inaugurated in 2004, is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Formula One grand prix held in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility stages various motorsport events including the annual Formula One race, GP2 Series competition, and 24-hour endurance races, with multiple track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km circuit near Montmeló features a balanced mix of straightaways and varied corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One teams. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near the Belgian town of Spa in Wallonia, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, except for 2003 and 2006, continuing a tradition that extends back to 1925 when it first welcomed motorsport competition.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that serves as the home venue for Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its use in top-tier single-seater racing, the circuit has welcomed various international motorsport series including sportscar championships and North American racing categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading hosts China's premier racing events, most notably the Chinese Grand Prix which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix since 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that has been the primary home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. Though the British Grand Prix alternated between three circuits during the 1955-1986 period, it has remained exclusively at Silverstone since 1987, which also stages the MotoGP British round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km racetrack located near Budapest that hosted Formula One's first grand prix within the Eastern Bloc in 1986, following Bernie Ecclestone's desire to establish a race in that region. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, making it the fastest-constructed Formula One circuit, the permanent facility replaced initial plans for a street course through the city's largest park, with the inaugural race dedicated to Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, ranking among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues and Europe's oldest on the mainland. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 with only a single interruption in 1980, it remains one of Formula One's most consistent fixtures and earns its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" through its characteristic long straights and high-velocity corner configurations.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting up to 155,000 spectators. The circuit serves as a premier venue for Formula One and Japanese Super Formula competitions, establishing itself as one of motorsport's most prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track navigates past some of the city's most iconic destinations, including major casino resorts and entertainment venues like MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards after a 23-year absence, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021, utilizing a revised track layout compared to its previous hosting periods.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track joined the championship calendar in 2022, and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix as its primary event.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track winding through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, skirting the Monaco harbour. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, the circuit is universally known as Monte Carlo because the majority of its layout occupies that particular area of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Situated in the Dutch coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km Dutch circuit made its Formula One comeback in 2021 after a long absence, hosting the revived Dutch Grand Prix until the partnership concluded in 2026. The track, nestled near the North Sea shoreline, has operated under various names throughout its history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a notably long main straight of over one kilometer. Holding FIA Grade 1 status, the track is protected by artificial grass barriers designed to prevent desert sand from affecting racing conditions.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, located in São Paulo, Brazil, is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate deceased Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The venue, which also features a kart track dedicated to Ayrton Senna, has hosted numerous Formula One grands prix since its establishment.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street course situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, hosting the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021 and welcoming Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay area to create a temporary racing venue.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing teams. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license and equipped with seating for over 140,000 spectators, this venue serves as a premier motorsport facility.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the primary venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major motorsport events including NASCAR races, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance competition, while previously accommodating various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai and British driver, races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him uniquely the only driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight race victories following his entry to the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish competitor, currently drives for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his racing career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while simultaneously racing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. Between 2024 and 2025, he participated in seven Formula One Grands Prix.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The French driver previously achieved a significant victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, holding seven World Championship titles that equal Michael Schumacher's record. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand driver currently racing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season career in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with WRT for BMW, while also running part-time in NASCAR for Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, with appearances from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight-season career, he has achieved 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One after previously competing for Alpine, where he achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac after spending 15 seasons in the sport during which he secured six race victories. He achieved his career-best championship result by finishing second in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories over the course of four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" throughout his career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories over his eight seasons competing in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant, an American driver, previously competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 class with Proton Competition, having previously raced in the LMP2 category of IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive world championships with Red Bull Racing between 2021 and 2024, establishing himself as one of Formula One's most dominant competitors. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories while continuing his tenure with the energy drink team.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver in Formula One, currently fulfilling a reserve role with Cadillac. He previously competed in the championship from 2022 through 2024, making him the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the sport's elite category.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Based at Enstone, this team operated as Renault's factory outfit since 2021 under the Alpine brand name, following a rebranding from its previous Renault F1 identity. The squad maintained its connection to the French manufacturer throughout its tenure, ending Renault's works team involvement at the close of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has a long-standing presence in Formula One through multiple team incarnations, with the current racing operation run by AMR GP Limited competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury car manufacturer, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, participating in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Widely recognized by their iconic "Prancing Horse" emblem, the team has established an unmatched legacy of success throughout the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-based Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, debuting competitively in 2016. The organization is currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from Guenther Steiner following the latter's departure in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering outfit, established in 1970, became a renowned independent Formula One constructor after joining the grid in 1993. Prior to its motorsport evolution, the team achieved significant success in endurance racing, including victory at Le Mans in 1989. The organization competed for over three decades as one of the sport's longest-serving teams before its acquisition by Audi in 2024 marked the end of its independent operations.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. From 2022, ownership became equally shared between the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff, while the squad maintains its traditional "Silver Arrows" identity in the sport.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor based in Faenza that entered the championship in 2024 as the second team owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. The outfit maintains facilities in both Italy and Milton Keynes, operating as a sister team within the Red Bull Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian racing licence, has been a Formula One competitor since 2005 as part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its twenty-year history until Laurent Mekies took over team management in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, has become one of the sport's most prominent teams. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team evolved from Williams's previous racing endeavor and competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team. The organization operates from a substantial manufacturing facility that has supported decades of championship competition.
